title: Government revenue and tax
competency: Explain government revenue and tax, list their benefits and describe the history of tax in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: All the income of the government from taxes and non-tax sources.
A compulsory fee a government charges people or organizations to pay for public works and services.

en.text: Government revenue is all the government's income from taxes and non-tax sources; it pays for roads, schools and services. Tax is a compulsory charge. Benefits include reducing inequality, economic stability, fewer regional imbalances, capital accumulation, jobs and encouraging exports. Ethiopian taxes go back to Axum, Zera Yaqob and Menelik II's fixed tithe.

screens.title: Revenue and tax
paras: Government revenue is all the income of the government from taxes and non-tax sources.
It is used for government spending.
Tax is a compulsory fee charged on people or organizations.
Taxes pay for public works and services such as roads and schools.

screens.title: Benefits of revenue and tax
paras: Governments need large revenue for economic and social activities.
table: Reducing gaps in income and wealth
Using tax to help poorer regions

screens.title: History of tax in Ethiopia
paras: Traditional taxes were on crops, livestock, wool, butter and milk; elephant hunters paid ivory tax.
Axum had traditional taxation. King Zera Yaqob (1434–1468) introduced the first tax system.
Menelik II set a fixed tithe instead of arbitrary farm taxes.
Later regimes changed income, land and other taxes.
table: Income, land, education, health, road, salt and other taxes
Land taxes and tithe abolished; rural land-use fee of birr 5, 10, or 2 per hectare
First birr 105 of monthly income exempt; later birr 120
